disk_estimate.status: Calculated payload and illustrative transfers; no completed disk-cache benchmark
disk_estimate.attention_payload_formula: 16 layers * 2 arrays * 4 KV heads * 256 head dimension * 2 bytes; target attention KV only, summed across both GPUs
disk_estimate.assumptions: One complete read of the attention cache at the stated hypothetical sustained storage bandwidth. Not an output-token rate. Excludes computation, recurrent/draft state, padding, metadata, and additional unoverlapped transfer. Partial residence, pipelining and speculative acceptance change the model calculation.
disk_estimate.streaming_status: Not implemented or benchmarked in the cited experiments

timing_analysis.method: Wall time and tool time from saved run records. Reading estimated from cold-read rates; writing is a residual and includes call overhead. Summary-call times are estimated. No per-token timestamps or isolated disk-I/O measurements.

cache_reuse.method: Common prefixes measured in rendered characters and converted to tokens with per-call ratios; not exact tokenization.

cache_break_even.method: Counterfactual calculation from saved calls and measured/assumed cold-read rates; not a paired cache-off run.

edit_cost.about: Wait before the first output token after one edit (a deletion) inside a cached prompt, exact prefix cache on. first_edit_s: first request after the edit; repeat_s: the same edited prompt sent again; cold_s: the same prompt with nothing cached. Fill a cell by setting status to "measured" and the three times, then run scripts/organize_results.py and scripts/build_site.py.

distance_probes.question: An agent works on one task whose history is many times larger than its live window. Questions planted at known distances back (counted in batches, called items in the evidence files) show what each way of managing the window still remembers, and whether it still follows a rule and a method stated at the start. The keeper section asks whether something outside the agent can do that managing. The in-place and retrieval sections ask how cheaply the keeper's notes can be kept, and what retrieval alone does on the same streams. The harder-stream entry asks what notes and retrieval do together on text that refers to things indirectly. The entries of 2026-10-12 ask whether the fast form of the notes can be moved into the proxy without losing answers or speed, and whether a rule that names nothing it covers separates notes from retrieval.
distance_probes.task: Sparse prose stream: about 240K tokens (240,208 on seed 0, in 147 batches), about 3 counter changes per batch. Every 25 batches a probe asks three questions about a batch further back: a counter's current value, an earlier value that was later overwritten, and who did a particular thing. Final questions at the end: 14 on seed 0, 21 on seed 1.
distance_probes.model: Qwen3.8-27B, FP8 weights, 16-bit attention cache, exact prefix cache, drafting on, tool calling on, one request at a time

methods.window: Window-drop (lossy): when over the cap, drop the oldest turns. Nothing is kept.
methods.compaction: Compaction (lossy), as coding agents do it: replace old tool output with a stub and strip old thinking, then drop the oldest turns.
methods.self_edit_read: Self-editing, read mode: the model reads each batch and keeps `name value` lines in a pinned state; processed batches leave the window.
methods.archive: Self-editing plus archive and search: the same pinned state, and every dropped batch goes word for word to a read-only archive the model can search with a `recall` tool.
methods.archive_rules: Archive and search with pinned rule lines: the pinned state may also hold permanent `RULE:` lines; an edit that removes or rewords one is rejected, and the instructions say to add a rule or method when one is stated and to read the RULE lines before answering.
methods.archive_free: Archive and search with free-text notes: free-text notes instead of `name value` lines. Its instructions say nothing about rules.
methods.summary: Summarise at a threshold (lossy), the method most production agents use: when the context reaches 75% of the window, the model writes a summary that takes the place of the older turns.
methods.keeper: Keeper: the agent manages nothing. When the conversation is about to outgrow the window, the test harness writes the oldest turns word for word to an archive, asks the model once, with no tools, to rewrite a short NOTES block (RULES, STATE, OPEN) from the old notes and the turns about to go, puts back any rule the model left out, and replaces those turns with the NOTES. The model can search the archive with a `recall` tool, and the RULES are repeated beside every set of questions.
methods.keeper_proxy: Keeper as a proxy: the same policy in a small OpenAI-compatible proxy in front of the model server. The agent sends its whole history on every call and manages nothing; the proxy keeps the live window at 32K, and its archive and notes live outside the task sandbox.
methods.keeper_inplace: Keeper with in-place notes: the same keeper with a cheaper way to keep its NOTES. Every ten items the note-taking call is the conversation the server has already read, with one more message at its end. The model replies with the changes only, the harness applies and checks them, and every turn in view then goes to the archive, so the window starts again from the task and the NOTES.
methods.retrieval: Retrieval only ("RAG"): no notes, no pinned rules, no search tool. Every item goes into a store as it arrives; when an item asks questions the harness shows the best-matching stored sentences for each question, each with the sentence after it (keyword matching).
methods.keeper_inplace_retrieval: Keeper with in-place notes and retrieval at question time: the same keeper, and whenever an item asks questions the harness also shows the best-matching stored sentences for each question, each with the sentence after it (keyword matching, 20 per question).
methods.keeper_proxy_inplace: Keeper as a proxy, with in-place notes: the proxy takes its notes the way the harness keeper with in-place notes does. The note-taking call is the view the server has just read, without the newest exchange, plus one message; the reply holds only what changed; the proxy checks and applies it, archives the noted messages word for word, and the view becomes the opening messages, the NOTES and the newest exchange.

lessons.lesson: The request for notes must come after the turns being removed, not before.
lessons.from: Asked first, with about 8K tokens of the agent's own turns after the request, the model continued its own turns, wrote no RULES section, and the rule was gone after the first cut. That run was stopped after two minutes.

lessons.lesson: A rule needs a pinned place and a reminder at the point of use.
lessons.from: With no pinned place four methods answered 0/20 rule questions. Pinned only, the rule was applied 22 times out of 29 over 1M tokens. Pinned and repeated beside the questions: 29/29.

lessons.lesson: Thinking must stay on while a question is open.
lessons.from: In the first 1M attempt thinking was on for the call that received a question set and off for the calls after it; the model repeated one archive search 790 times.

The note-taking call sends the same reasoning effort as the other calls and has more room; a rejected notes reply is asked for again without thinking; when a turn has used up its archive searches the model is asked once more without the tool. Seed 1 went from 42/46 in 47 minutes to 44/46 in 18 with no note-taking call rejected (10 of 24 before); seed 0 from 37/39 in 21 minutes to 39/39 in 17.

in_place.question: Can the fast form of the keeper (in-place notes) be moved out of the test harness into the proxy, for an agent that sends its whole history and manages nothing, without losing answers or speed?
in_place.what: Keeper as a proxy, with in-place notes: the proxy takes its notes the way the harness keeper with in-place notes does. The note-taking call is the view the server has just read, without the newest exchange, plus one message; the reply holds only what changed; the proxy checks and applies it, archives the noted messages word for word, and the view becomes the opening messages, the NOTES and the newest exchange.
in_place.differences_from_the_harness_keeper: Forced by a client that resends its history: the newest exchange stays in view (the model has to act on it), so about nine items are noted per call instead of ten; the latest user message stays in view while it is being worked on; a question that arrived in a tool result blocks the cut until it is closed.
in_place.agent: A plain agent with no context management of its own. It sends its whole history on every call.
in_place.minutes: Whole-job minutes as the lab note gives them. The minutes column of the evidence tables counts the agent only and reads lower for the proxy runs.

builds.label: First build
builds.what: In-place notes in the proxy as first written.
builds.outcome: On the second stream a reply that had been asked for again replaced the first one. It held four lines where the first held 27, so the changes of nine batches were lost: 40 of 46, with 15 values wrong in the notes.

builds.label: Second build: replies are merged
builds.what: A reply that is asked for again replaces only the lines of the names it mentions; every other line of the reply before it stays.
builds.outcome: Every answer right on both 240K streams. Over 1,000,000 tokens it missed the bar set beforehand on both counts: six answers blank and six wrong.

builds.label: Third build: fixes from the first million-token run
builds.what: Search hits show the first line of their message; the searches of a turn that ended empty are carried into the next request; note lines are counted and followed by their parts; every amount in a line's working must be stated in the turns.
builds.outcome: Faster, and it failed the check set before the long run. Both low scores come from one weak point: a questioned note got no usable answer and the whole step fell back to the full rewrite. The 1,000,000-token run was not made on this build.

builds.label: Fourth build: a questioned reply stands
builds.what: A questioned reply never falls back to the full rewrite: the first reply stands without the questioned lines. A line for a name the noted turns never mention is left out. The notes request says what the first message after the NOTES is.
builds.outcome: Every answer right on both 240K streams, with nothing wrong in the notes. Over 1,000,000 tokens it met the bar. Six of its eight misses, probably seven, are one mix-up between message numbers and item numbers in the search tool.

builds.label: Fifth build, the current one: the search tool counts in the stream’s own numbers
builds.what: The search tool shows and takes the content's own item numbers and nothing else; when there are more matches than fit, the nearest ones are shown and the line that says so comes first; a misspelled name is given to the name it was meant for.
builds.outcome: Within two answers of the keeper inside the test harness, and as fast.

lessons.lesson: Results that only the proxy saw must not be lost when a turn ends empty.
lessons.from: The proxy answers the model's archive searches itself, so the agent's history never holds them. At one question item the model made its eight searches and then returned an empty reply; in the next request everything found was gone, and six answers were never written.
lessons.fix: The searches of a turn that ended with nothing for the client are shown again in the next request, and an empty reply is asked for once more with thinking off.

lessons.lesson: A search tool must count one way.
lessons.from: Hits were labelled with message numbers while the questions speak of item numbers: six wrong answers about a numbered item. Then each hit showed both, and the model asked for everything "before 332" meaning item 332 and got everything before message 332, which is item 150. It trusted that search over its own correct notes: six more wrong answers, probably seven.
lessons.fix: The tool can run in the content's own numbering: every number it shows or takes is then an item number. With it, every earlier-value question was right (58/58).

lessons.lesson: A list that is cut short has to say so first.
lessons.from: "The first 40 of 63", with the note at the end, was read as all there is.
lessons.fix: A cut-off list says so in its first line and shows the matches nearest to what was asked for.

lessons.lesson: What stays in view after a cut gets written down twice.
lessons.from: The proxy keeps the newest exchange in view so that a real agent can still see what it has just fetched. The model's remark in that exchange was about the result before it, already in the notes; at the next notes call it noted those changes again, once the wrong way round (an 84 that had been added was taken away).
lessons.fix: The notes request says what that first message is, and a line for a name that none of the noted turns mentions is left out.

lessons.lesson: A questioned note must never fall back to a slower, different path.
lessons.from: When the model gave no usable answer to a question about its notes, the whole cut was redone with a full rewrite. In one run that lost a change. In another the rewrite added a "rule" that restated the task's opening message; rules are repeated at every question item, and at the last one the model followed it literally and overwrote a file holding 25 right answers: 14/39 where the next build scored 39/39.
lessons.fix: The first reply stands, without the questioned lines.

lessons.lesson: A model told to show its working will invent working.
lessons.from: "The clerk recorded katu85 at five hundred and twenty-three" came back as 650 - 27 = 623. It adds up and starts from the value held, so the checks passed it.
lessons.fix: Every amount in a line's working has to be stated in the text. Not caught yet: a value that was set, noted as a change by that same number.

lessons.lesson: A safety rule can be too eager.
lessons.from: "A line whose number the turns do not state is left out" also left out three lines that were right or nearly right but written in a form the checker could not follow. Their counters kept stale values; the two wrong counters that were the rule's doing cost no answer.
lessons.fix: A line is left out only for a number the turns contradict, never because the checker lost its way. Unit-tested; not yet run on the streams.

lessons.lesson: The server kept being stopped at the end of long runs, and it was not the run.
lessons.from: A script that summarises results held every saved snapshot of a trial at once: 1.7 GB on disk after a 1M proxy run, beside a model server with about 2 GB of host memory to spare.
lessons.fix: One snapshot is held at a time: 50 MB.

lessons.lesson: New checking code is read by a second reviewer before it runs.
lessons.from: Five reviews in one day found 46 issues, several of which would have stored a wrong value. One morning fix ran before its review, because the usual reviewer cannot run beside the busy model server.
lessons.fix: A reviewer that only reads can run beside the server, so the review no longer has to wait for the cards.

in_place.question: Where does the keeper's time go, and can its notes be kept at lower cost without losing answers?
in_place.what: In-place notes. Every ten items the note-taking call is the conversation the server has already read, with one more message at its end asking what those turns changed. The model replies with the changes only, written with thinking on. The harness applies them to the NOTES and checks them. Then every turn in view is moved to the archive, so the window starts again from the task and the NOTES and nothing has to be read back.
checks: Every mention of a tracked name in the turns being moved out must be accounted for by a line of changes.
A worked-out value must show its working, and the working must start from the value the NOTES hold.
The harness redoes every sum. A reply that fails a check is asked for again in place.

where_the_time_went.run: The keeper's finished 1M run with a full notes rewrite at each cut (arm N32j)
where_the_time_went.server: Over the 1,170 requests of this campaign the server spent 54% of its time reading and 46% writing. With a full notes rewrite every piece of the stream was read about four times: when it arrived, again when the turns kept after a cut were read back, and again when the turns being cut were shown to the note-taking call.

full_rewrite.note: The published keeper, timed to one decimal for this comparison. The keeper rows above give the same two 240K runs as 15 and 16 minutes.

rows.new_in_this_version: In-place notes that think, every ten items.
A doubtful reply is asked for again in place; a noted value is read as its last number.
A name the items mention must have a line of changes.
The lines of a name must account for as many changes as the items mention it.
A value written without working must be one the items state.
Every check. Digits inside a name are not numbers the items state, and a value written without working must be stated in a sentence that names the thing, or the one after it.
Every check. Digits inside a name are not numbers the items state, and a value written without working must be stated in a sentence that names the thing, or the one after it.

audit.tool: Every saved version of the NOTES is compared with the grader's true ledger at the point that version covers. The count is the counters whose noted value was ever wrong. A wrong value can sit in the NOTES without costing an answer if nothing asks for that counter before it is set again.
audit.without_thinking: Notes written without thinking: about 570 tokens a call instead of 1,865. Six runs on the first 240K stream scored 39, 39, 36, 39, 38 and 39 of 39, and every one had 2 to 8 counters wrong in its NOTES at some point. Not adopted.
audit.example: "The clerk recorded domo86 at three hundred and forty-two. ... Ten were taken from domo86." was noted as -390 - 342 - 10 = -742: a set read as a subtraction. The true value was 332. The value stayed wrong for 35 items, until the next set, and no question asked for it in between.
audit.full_rewrite_at_1m: At one cut of the full-rewrite keeper's 1M run its rewritten NOTES ended mid-list, 39 lines instead of 62, and five live counters were missing until later cuts brought them back. Its score (226/228) had not shown it. Changes applied by the harness cannot lose lines that way: every line the model does not mention is kept.

retrieval_only.question: How does the keeper differ from retrieval alone ("RAG"): a store that holds everything, with the best matches shown when a question arrives?
retrieval_only.what: No notes, no pinned rules, no search tool. Every item goes into a store as it arrives. When an item asks questions, the harness shows the best-matching stored sentences for each question, each with the sentence after it: 20 per question on the 240K streams, 40 on the 1M stream. Items that only ask questions are not stored.
retrieval_only.retriever: Keyword matching (BM25 over sentences). This is the favourable retriever for this text, where the things asked about are exact names. No embedding retriever was tested: there is no room for one beside the model on this host.

builds.first: The store held only what had left the window.
builds.second: The store held every item from the moment it arrived, but the model could reach the stored files itself.
builds.final: The store holds every item from the moment it arrives and is kept out of the model's reach.

lessons_from_the_builds: The store must hold everything from the moment it arrives. When it held only what had left the window the model did not put the two together: 7 of 14 final questions right, four of the misses stale values, though every sentence a right answer needed was in front of it.

The model must not be able to reach the store itself. In the second build it found the stored files and answered the final questions with its own scripts: right on the first stream bar one, and on the second with a number parser that added about 100 to most values (5 of 21).

lessons.lesson: A refused repeat does not end a loop.
lessons.from: The same context plus the same refusal gives the same command again. The fully checked keeper sent one archive search 362 times in a row at the first question item, was refused each time, and scored 3/50.
lessons.fix: From the third refusal in a row the refusal says to stop and answer, and that one call is sampled.

lessons.lesson: A search tool that prints matching sentences alone is blind on text that says "it".
lessons.from: A search for a counter's name returned "Next on the list was nipewe33." and never the sentence after it, which held the change.
lessons.fix: The archive search prints each match with the sentence after it.

lessons.lesson: A loop can go round three commands.
lessons.from: With repeats refused, the model circled between three different searches; that run was stopped by hand at 11 minutes.
lessons.fix: A search sent a third time since the last item arrived is refused like a repeat: the archive has not changed in between.

lessons.lesson: A reply that is asked for again must not lose what the first reply had.
lessons.from: The first note-taking reply named the standing rule, a check asked for the reply again, the second reply left the rule out, and the second reply stood. The rule was lost at the first cut (3/5 rule questions in the voided run).
lessons.fix: A rule named in any reply of one note-taking call is kept (5/5 again in the next run).

hard_stream.reading: On text that refers to things indirectly the two together beat either alone: 47/50 and 46/50 with retrieval added to the keeper, 42/50 (and 43/50 in a voided run) with notes only, and retrieval alone too slow to finish. One seed: this says which way the difference points, no more. A second seed on 2026-10-12 gave 46/49 with retrieval added; its partner run without retrieval did not finish, so the comparison is still one seed.

retrieval_only.correction: Before these runs we expected retrieval alone to lose the standing rule. On this test it did not at 240K: the rule names the counters it covers, so a question about one of them retrieves it. The expectation came from the earlier archive method, in which the model decides when to search. The rule was lost only late in the 1M stream (4 times in 29). A rule that names nothing it covers was tested on 2026-10-12 and there the expectation held: unnamed_rule.
retrieval_only.reading: Retrieval finds things; notes hold what must always be in view (rules, current state) at a fixed size. The keeper has both: its archive search is retrieval on demand. Automatic retrieval at question time added to the keeper was run in campaign 10b: on the harder stream the two together scored 47/50 and 46/50 against 42/50 for notes alone, and on the second ordinary 240K stream 46/46 in 11.2 minutes. A rule that names nothing it covers shows the difference directly: the keeper applied it 16/16 times, retrieval alone 0/16.

On the harder stream the comparison with and without retrieval is one seed and not calibrated. The stream with a rule that names nothing has one ambiguous clause (tallies below zero). The keeper with retrieval added has not been run at 1M. One synthetic task family, one model, one machine.

unnamed_rule.question: Does a rule that names nothing it covers separate notes from retrieval?
unnamed_rule.task: The 240K rule-and-method stream with one more rule in item 1: "any figure below zero is reported as the single word overdrawn, never as a number", for every answer about a counter, now or earlier, and the final list. It names no counter and shares no word with the questions it governs. 7 of 39 expected answers on seed 0 and 9 of 46 on seed 1 are that word.
unnamed_rule.reading_rule_set_before_the_runs: "Kept" at 80% or more of the governed questions, "lost" at 20% or less.
unnamed_rule.what_retrieval_answered: The true negative number, all 16 times. The rule had left the window by the first question item, and nothing in "What value does X hold now?" leads a search back to it.
unnamed_rule.what_the_keeper_did: The rule was a RULES line from the first cut, whole, and it was repeated at every question item.
unnamed_rule.stream_fault: The rule's last clause, "a tally is still worked out from the true figure", does not say how a tally that comes out below zero is to be reported. The keeper, with the rule in view, answered "overdrawn" for four such tallies; the grader expects the number. Those four are all of the keeper's misses outside the governed questions. Retrieval, which had lost the rule, gave the number and was marked right.
unnamed_rule.why_the_earlier_comparison_could_not_sho: There the rule named its counters, so a search for a counter found the rule.
unnamed_rule.limit: Two streams, one run per cell, one synthetic task family. The two keeper runs are two states of the code.
